thread:
deploy-bot: Starting gradual rollout of model 'redwood-open-2.1' to canary (10 nodes). manifest checksum: sha256:DEF456... deployed artifact hash: sha256:ABC123... initiating canary. /deploy id=deploy_2026_03_15_01

carter: seeing 500s on the canary group — responses include 'tokenizer mismatch' and garbled tokens. Noticing repeated <||> tokens and truncated outputs.

devops-bot: Paging SRE oncall @lina — automatic anomaly detect triggered (err-rate spike + checksum mismatch).

lina: Ack — I'm oncall. Pulling canary logs now. Which region?

carter: eu-west-1 canaries first. Quick log dump:
```
2026-03-15T01:03:12Z ERROR modelloader: weight bundle checksum mismatch expected=sha256:DEF456 actual=sha256:ABC123
2026-03-15T01:03:12Z ERROR modelloader: aborting load, raising ValueError('weights checksum mismatch')
2026-03-15T01:03:13Z ERROR tokenizer: vocab size mismatch expected=50258 got=50257
2026-03-15T01:03:13Z WARN inference: returned 500, body: "tokenizer mismatch: unknown token id 50257"
```

sophia: on the registry side I see two uploads within the same minute for redwood-open-2.1. One was the CI-published artifact (sha256:DEF456) then a manual reupload (sha256:ABC123). Looks like the manual upload replaced the artifact without updating the manifest. Checking who pushed.

lina: Severity assessment — customer-facing errors observed, spike in 500s on canaries. Recommend kill-switch + rollback to be safe. @ops-oncall please flip the route flag and start rollback.

ops-oncall: Executing kill-switch now for route 'routes/model-open-2.1' -> off. Command used: `./infra/flagsctl set model_open_2_1.enabled false --by ops-oncall --reason "checksum mismatch"`

deploy-bot: Feature flag toggled: model_open_2_1.enabled=false by ops-oncall. Starting automated rollback: target version redwood-open-2.0. Rolling back canaries first.

carter: Running rollback command: `/deploy rollback --deploy-id deploy_2026_03_15_01 --to-version redwood-open-2.0 --strategy canary`

mia: CS: creating an incident ticket and notifying impacted customers. Early estimate ~0.9% of requests between 01:02-01:05 UTC produced malformed completions. Ticket #CS-7892. Sending outreach to top 5 affected customers now.

lina: Observability update: traffic draining from v2 canaries, v1 instances ramping, error-rate back to baseline within 3 minutes of rollback. No further tokenizer errors seen after 01:06 UTC.

sophia: Initial root-cause hypothesis: publish step did not enforce artifact -> manifest checksum parity. The manual reupload replaced the weight bundle but did not trigger a manifest revision. Deploy consumed the (reuploaded) artifact whose tokenizer files were not updated to match weights.

carter: quick mitigation notes saved in incident log. Also saw some stack traces referencing `model_loader.verify_checksum()` failing — putting those traces into the incident doc.

lina: Handoff / next steps:
- Postmortem (owner: lina) due 2026-03-18
- CI publish gate: enforce checksum verification between weight bundle and manifest (owner: sophia) due 2026-03-17
- Deploy canary validation: synthetic tokenization parity check pre-traffic (owner: carter) due 2026-03-20
- Block reuploads during live deploys (owner: infra-team) due 2026-03-22

devops-bot: Handoff: SRE oncall @lina handing to @ops-oncall for follow-ups. Incident state: mitigated, rollback complete.

customer-success: CS outreach sent, customers received notice and SLAs were offered where appropriate. Ticket #CS-7892 updated with timeline and rollback confirmation.

carter: :thumbsup: thanks everyone — attaching additional logs to the incident doc.

lina: Filing the incident doc now and will schedule the blameless postmortem. If folks have any extra evidence (CI history, who did manual upload), drop here or attach to the doc.

sophia: Found the manual upload user: build-admin-bot triggered by a queued manual job at 01:01:50 UTC. Adding that to timeline.

mia: CS: noted. We'll follow up with affected customers after the postmortem.

lina: Closing thread for real-time mitigation. Postmortem link will be shared in #postmortems. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
